quick: Monarch caterpillars can eat only milkweeds. Those plants are therefore not just nectar sources — they are the nursery on which the next generation depends. Florida is different: some monarchs remain and breed through winter rather than joining the long-distance migration. Many monarchs from eastern North America migrate thousands of miles to mountain forests in central Mexico, where they spend the winter in enormous colonies. The round trip spans several generations. The late-summer migratory generation lives much longer than summer monarchs and makes the long southbound journey; later generations continue the return north. Milkweeds contain defensive chemicals called cardenolides. Monarch caterpillars store some of them in their bodies, which can make the caterpillars and adult butterflies distasteful or toxic to some predators.
